reuse.why: Reuses the existing assertBankAccountNotLinked guard that every provider already calls, and extracts unlinkAccount's field-clearing update into clearAccountLink so the takeover leaves the old account exactly as unlinking does.

duplication.why: The unlink field set is now defined once and shared by unlinkAccount and the takeover; no logic is copied.

placement.why: The takeover's write (clearing the other account's link) is hidden inside a function named and used as an assertion, so a check now mutates the database before the link itself runs, instead of the replace step living in the link flow (e.g. linkAccountAndSync).

scope.why: Only the flag, its threading through the six providers, the shared clear helper and one test are changed.

maintainability.why: Behaviour is centralised, but an 'assert' with side effects is surprising, and the flag must be threaded by hand through six provider functions and positional arguments.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All providers go through assertBankAccountNotLinked and unlinkAccount uses the new clearAccountLink.

disguised_duplication.where: The unlink update was extracted and shared, not copied.
